$comment: Single source of truth for the OPC UA MCP tool and resource surface shared by both servers. The Node server builds its tools/list response directly from this file (copied into build/ at build time). The Python (FastMCP) server reads tool descriptions and the capability node IDs from it; its signature-derived input schemas are checked against this file by tests/test_contract_parity.py. To add or change a tool: edit this file, then update each server's per-tool logic (Node: a case in the CallTool switch; Python: the @mcp.tool function), and add an E2E test. A tool whose output is more than free text also names a shape from "resultShapes"; tests/e2e/test_contract_parity.py checks both servers' actual output against it. The "resources" key does the same for MCP resources: both servers build their resources/list from it, and the parity test reads each resource and checks its document against the shape its "body" names.

resultShapes.$comment: Canonical response shapes, referenced by a tool's "resultShape". Both servers must produce the referenced shape verbatim: a client (or a model) that learns one server's output must be able to read the other's. See issue #23.

historyRecords.$comment: Returned as one MCP text content block per record, each block the JSON object described by "items". An empty result is zero blocks. The Python server additionally returns the array as structured content.

value.description: The recorded value, encoded per its OPC UA data type: numbers, booleans and strings stay themselves; a ByteString is base64; a DateTime is ISO-8601 UTC; a Guid is a lower-case UUID; NodeId, StatusCode, QualifiedName and LocalizedText are their canonical text forms; an Int64/UInt64 outside the range a JSON number can hold exactly, and a non-finite Double, become strings ("9007199254740993", "NaN"); an array value is a JSON array of those. null for an interval the server holds no data for. The full table, and the fact that both servers produce the same encoding for the same reading, is pinned by tests/fixtures/value-encoding.json.

timestamp.description: Source timestamp, ISO-8601 UTC with a trailing 'Z'. Example: '2026-09-09T13:36:01.468Z'. null when the server supplied none.

status.description: OPC UA status code name. Examples: 'Good', 'BadNoData'.

subscriptionRecords.$comment: Returned as one MCP text content block per record, each block the JSON object described by "items" — the same framing as "historyRecords". `subscribe_opcua_node` returns the one subscription it created; `list_subscriptions` returns every active one, and zero blocks when there are none. The `opcua://subscriptions` resource carries the same records under its "subscriptions" key.

subscription_id.description: Handle for this subscription, unique within the running MCP server. Pass it to `unsubscribe_opcua_node`. Example: 'sub-1'.

node_id.description: The OPC UA node being monitored. Example: 'ns=2;i=3'.

publishing_interval.description: How often (ms) the OPC UA server was asked to publish queued changes.

sampling_interval.description: How often (ms) the OPC UA server was asked to sample the node. Equal to `publishing_interval` when the caller left it at 0.

buffer_size.description: How many of the most recent changes this subscription retains. Older ones are discarded.

change_count.description: Total data changes received since subscribing, including any discarded by the buffer. An OPC UA server sends the node's current value as the first change, so this reaches 1 without the value having moved.

changes.description: The retained changes, oldest first, at most `buffer_size` of them. Each is a record of the shape defined by "historyRecords": { value, timestamp, status }.

resources.$comment: MCP resources both servers expose. A resource is re-readable state rather than an action, which is what makes it the right home for live subscription data: an agent can refresh it without spending a tool call. Change *notifications* are deliberately not sent — see docs/architecture.md.
resources.name: opcua_subscriptions
resources.description: Active OPC UA data-change subscriptions and the values buffered for each. Re-read after `subscribe_opcua_node` to see what has changed.

body.$comment: The document is a JSON object with one key, whose value is an array of records of the named result shape. The parity test reads the resource from both servers and checks it against this.

tools.name: read_opcua_node
tools.description: Read the value of a specific OPC UA node

node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID in the format 'ns=<namespace>;i=<identifier>'. Example: 'ns=2;i=2'.

tools.name: write_opcua_node
tools.description: Write a value to a specific OPC UA node

node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID in the format 'ns=<namespace>;i=<identifier>'. Example: 'ns=2;i=3'.

value.description: The value to write to the node. Will be converted based on node type.

tools.name: browse_opcua_node_children
tools.description: Browse the children of a specific OPC UA node

node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID to browse (e.g., 'ns=0;i=85' for Objects folder).

tools.name: read_multiple_opcua_nodes
tools.description: Read the values of multiple OPC UA nodes in a single request

node_ids.description: A list of OPC UA node IDs to read (e.g., ['ns=2;i=2', 'ns=2;i=3']).

tools.name: write_multiple_opcua_nodes
tools.description: Write values to multiple OPC UA nodes in a single request

nodes_to_write.description: A list of objects containing 'node_id' and 'value'. Example: [{'node_id': 'ns=2;i=2', 'value': '10.5'}, {'node_id': 'ns=2;i=3', 'value': 'active'}]

tools.name: call_opcua_method
tools.description: Call a method on a specific OPC UA object node

object_node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID of the object that contains the method. Example: 'ns=2;i=1' for the Methods folder.

method_node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID of the method to call. Example: 'ns=2;i=2' for StartProduction method.

arguments.description: List of arguments to pass to the method. Arguments will be converted to appropriate OPC UA variants.

tools.name: get_all_variables
tools.description: Get all available variables from the OPC UA server, excluding those under the built-in 'Server' object

tools.name: subscribe_opcua_node
tools.description: Subscribe to data changes on a specific OPC UA node. The OPC UA server pushes each new value into a buffer this MCP server keeps; re-read it with `list_subscriptions` or the `opcua://subscriptions` resource instead of polling `read_opcua_node`

node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID to monitor, in the format 'ns=<namespace>;i=<identifier>'. Example: 'ns=2;i=3'.

publishing_interval.description: How often (ms) the OPC UA server publishes queued changes. Default 1000. Clamped to at least 50.

sampling_interval.description: How often (ms) the OPC UA server samples the node. 0 (the default) means sample at `publishing_interval`; a shorter interval queues several readings per publish.

buffer_size.description: How many of the most recent changes to retain for this subscription; older ones are discarded. Default 20, clamped to 1..1000.

tools.name: list_subscriptions
tools.description: List the active OPC UA data-change subscriptions, each with the value changes buffered for it since it was created

tools.name: unsubscribe_opcua_node
tools.description: Cancel an active OPC UA data-change subscription and discard its buffered changes

subscription_id.description: The subscription ID returned by `subscribe_opcua_node`, as listed by `list_subscriptions`. Example: 'sub-1'.

tools.name: read_history_opcua_node
tools.description: Read the historical values of a specific OPC UA node

node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID in the format 'ns=<namespace>;i=<identifier>'. Example: 'ns=2;i=2'.

num_values.description: Number of values to read (default: unlimited)

tools.name: read_aggregate_opcua_node
tools.description: Calculate the historical aggregates over a defined time range, divided into smaller chunks defined by the `processing_interval` (in milliseconds). The server divides the [`start_time`, `end_time`] domain into these intervals, returning one aggregated value per interval

node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID in the format 'ns=<namespace>;i=<identifier>'. Example: 'ns=2;i=2'.

processing_interval.description: The duration (ms) for each computed value. If set to 0, the server calculates a single aggregate value for the entire range.
